analysis.title: September Jobs Recap: Snap back to reality
key_insights: Nonfarm payrolls rose 29k in September, below the 90k expectation and the prior month's 133k, which was revised down from 162k. Natixis calls it a normalization of an existing trend rather than a break.
The 3-month average of payroll gains is 51k and the yearly average is 41k. Both are above most estimates of the breakeven rate that would stabilize unemployment.

The unemployment rate edged up to 4.175% from 4.141% (rounds to 4.2%), while labor force participation rose from 61.6% to 61.8%. Natixis reads the rise as driven by higher participation, a positive sign.
Average hourly earnings rose 0.1% m/m and 3.0% y/y. Natixis says wage growth is below the already tepid trend of the past year, so the labor market is not adding to inflation pressure.
Natixis thinks the labor market is somewhat shakier than the headline numbers suggest, but broadly still fine.

The data does not change the Fed's broader calculus because inflation remains the main concern. Lower wages and a weaker jobs picture reduce the urgency to hike in October, and possibly December if inflation data cooperates.
Natixis expects this cycle to end with fewer hikes than the market currently prices and forecasts only one more rate increase.
